passage: After Saturday practice at the community sports club, Trisha's mum Deepika waited by the gate holding a paper bag. Trisha had been asking about proper shin guards since the start of term, and each time Deepika said, "Let's see after your exams." Trisha had stopped asking, wore her old cracked pair without complaint, and helped wash the club bibs. Now she opened the bag slowly. "Mum..." Her voice went wobbly. She ran her thumb along the smooth edge, then hugged Deepika, muddy socks and all. "I'll look after them properly," she said. The coach, packing away cones, smiled. Trisha put them on in the car and kept looking at them all the way home.

qa.q: Where did Deepika wait for Trisha?
qa.a: She waited by the gate of the community sports club.

qa.q: What was Trisha feeling as she opened the bag slowly?
qa.a: Overwhelming happiness and gratitude; her voice went wobbly and she hugged Deepika. ❤️

qa.q: What did the waiting give Trisha?
qa.a: It made the shin guards feel extra special, so she valued them and promised to look after them properly.

qa.q: How might Deepika have felt watching Trisha wait without complaining?
qa.a: Probably proud and touched, and glad to reward the patience she had seen.

grounding: A child who waited patiently is given a wanted item and values it more because of the wait.

passage:
Class 4 diary, Monday
Yusuf came in today holding a small telescope as if it were made of glass. He told the class his Abba bought it on Saturday. "I asked in March. He said wait till my birthday. I waited six months!"
Deepika asked if he wasn't angry about waiting. Yusuf thought and said, "At first. But now it feels more special. Abba saved for it. He works nights at the bakery."
At break he let every child have one careful look through it.
During art period I asked Yusuf to make a thank-you card for his Abba. He drew the moon and wrote, "Worth the wait." I have tucked it into his bag to take home.

qa.q: When did Yusuf first ask for the telescope?
How does Yusuf feel about the telescope after waiting?
qa.a: He feels grateful and proud, and says it feels more special because he waited.

qa.q: How did the class teacher help Yusuf show his gratitude?
qa.a: They asked him to make a thank-you card in art period and tucked it into his bag to take home.

qa.q: How might Abba feel when he reads "Worth the wait"?
qa.a: He would probably feel touched and proud, knowing his effort was noticed.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a boy who waited patiently for a gift valuing it more and understanding his father's effort behind it.

passage:
Friday
MY BAT CAME TODAY. Mummy said in January, "After exams, if you still want it." I kept the picture from the sports-shop leaflet in my geography book and looked at it every night. Some nights I was cross about waiting.
Today Mummy came home late from the office, and she was holding it. Real willow. It smelled of wood and oil. I hugged her so hard her glasses went crooked. 😊
Then I noticed she looked tired, and I remembered she had taken extra shifts this month. I made her tea (too much sugar, sorry Mummy).
My little sister Kavitha wants to hold the bat. I let her, for exactly one minute.
Vaibhav

qa.q: When did Mummy first say Vaibhav could have the bat?
qa.a: In January, for after exams, if Vaibhav still wanted it.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel when Mummy came home with the bat?
qa.a: Overjoyed and grateful, hugging her so hard her glasses went crooked.

qa.q: What did the waiting teach Vaibhav?
qa.a: To value the bat more and to notice the effort behind it, like Mummy's extra shifts.

qa.q: How might Mummy have felt when Vaibhav made her tea?
qa.a: Tired but touched, seeing that Vaibhav noticed her effort. 🤍

grounding: A child who waited patiently for a bat values it more and notices the parent's effort behind it.
